svg.title: HSM Core Service - Sequence Diagram
svg.desc: Request flow: clients through PlainID, encrypt/decrypt via HSM service (including the core dek_name reuse-vs-mint branch) with Redis cache and CEK rotation, auditor SPN direct access path, plus the Tier 3 Bulk PoC dek_name reuse flow (hsm-bulk-client to HSM Service's own /dek/issue and /dek/unwrap endpoints), its file-format interoperability with HSM Service's own /decrypt, and optional compress-before-encrypt, all guarded by CoreBulkFileInteropTest
svg.text: HSM Service SPN · write KV Secrets

g.text: STARTUP (at service init — not per request)
0a. fetch current_key → "alpha"; fetch cek-alpha → (CEK bytes, kv_version) [Service SPN · vault.azure.net]
0b. CEK-alpha bytes + kv_version + prev slot (beta, if exists) → DEKCache initialized · same across all pods
0c. asyncio.create_task(cek_reload_loop) → polls current_key every 30s · rotate(cek, slot, kv_ver) on change
CEK rotation: Rotation SVC writes inactive slot FIRST → updates current_key → pods detect within 30s · old {slot}:{old_ver}:* entries expire via TTL
Recovery: rotation svc rotates immediately on restart · Service SPN read-only · Rotation SPN write-only on KV Secrets (vault.azure.net)
POLICY CHECK (every client request must clear this gate first)
1. policy check (JWT + logged-in user identity)
2a. [DENY] — call blocked, never reaches HSM service
2b. [ALLOW] — JWT enriched with AD group claim
caller proceeds to HSM service
↳ ALLOW path assumed below · PBAC decision stays client-side — HSM service only sees the Bearer JWT (Entra ID, a caller-signed self-issued JWT, or a client cert via mTLS — see AUTHORIZATION.md)
ENCRYPT FLOW
3. POST /encrypt
{ plaintext, encoding, data_classification, end_user_id }
4. validate JWT · app_id · scope=encrypt
4a. [found: same app, or granted (scope=encrypt)] REUSE: unwrap existing edek_blob (DekCache hit, else KEK unwrap)
4b. [found, different app, NOT granted] 403 · [not found] MINT: gen fresh DEK, wrap via KEK, INSERT edek_record
5. wrap DEK [Service SPN · RSA-OAEP-256 · Managed HSM]
6. EDEK (wrapped DEK)
7. gen DEK + IV · AES-256-GCM encrypt plaintext
8. INSERT edek_record → hsm_crypto (edek_id, blob, algorithm…)
9. edek_id (UUID)
[REUSE rejoins here — same edek_id, no INSERT]
10. audit_log → Splunk / SIEM (app_id, end_user_id, edek_id, status)
11. { ciphertext } ← only field client stores
DECRYPT FLOW
12. POST /decrypt { ciphertext, end_user_id }
13. SELECT edek_record WHERE id = edek_id → hsm_crypto
14. { edek_blob, kek_version, owner_app_id, data_class }
15. grant check: same app → coarse app_grants → fine-grained app_dek_grants [scope=decrypt]
granted / denied
15a. GET {slot}:{kv_ver}:{edek_id} (current slot first, prev slot fallback)
HIT → cached DEK bytes (skip steps 16 & 17 — jump to step 18)
MISS → nil → continue to Managed HSM unwrap ↓
[MISS only]
16. unwrap DEK [Service SPN · RSA-OAEP-256 · Managed HSM]
17. raw DEK bytes [MISS]
16a. [MISS] SET {slot}:{kv_ver}:{edek_id} CEK-encrypted EX 60s
18. AES-256-GCM decrypt · zero DEK immediately
19. audit_log → Splunk / SIEM (app_id, end_user_id, edek_id, status)
20. { plaintext } ← only field client needs
CEK ROTATION FLOW (every 4h or immediately on recovery — no pod restart)
R1. gen new 32-byte CEK · write to inactive slot (e.g. cek-beta) [Rotation SPN · write · KV Secrets]
R2. KV Secrets returns new kv_version for beta slot
R3. update current_key → "beta" [Rotation SPN · write · AFTER slot bytes written]
R4. poll detects current_key="beta" + new kv_version [Service SPN · read · 30s poll]
R5. fetch cek-beta bytes + kv_version [KV Secrets → HSM Service]
R6. rotate(new_cek, "beta", kv_version) → promotes alpha:{old_ver}→prev · installs beta:{new_ver}→current
New MISS entries written as beta:{new_kv_ver}:{edek_id} · old alpha:{old_ver}:* expire via 60s TTL · dual-read covers ~30s convergence window
Rotation SVC down at 4h mark: pods hold current CEK indefinitely · no errors · rotates immediately on recovery
AUDIT / SCAN FLOW (Auditor SPN — direct path, bypasses HSM service entirely)
21. get secrets: cek-alpha, cek-beta [KV Secrets · read-only · no Managed HSM access · crosses subscription boundary]
22. secret metadata (kv_version, content_type, attributes)
23. SELECT * FROM hsm_crypto + hsm_access [read-only · outside subscription]
24. edek records (wrapped blobs only)
Audit trail: Azure KV Diagnostic Logs + Splunk (separate pipeline) · Auditor reads KV Secrets only — no Managed HSM wrap/unwrap RBAC
Auditor SPN: no write access to any DB table · Redis cache not accessible · never routes through /decrypt endpoint
TIER 3: dek_name REUSE (hsm-bulk-client → HSM Service's own /dek/issue · /dek/unwrap — not a separate codebase)
hsm-bulk-client (CLNT)
HSM Service (SVC endpoints)
25. POST /dek/issue { key, data_classification, name: dek_name } [Bearer: static, Workload Identity, or self-signed JWT]
26. SVC: lookup by current_dek_name (GLOBAL — V14, was per-app)
26a. [FOUND, same app or granted] reuse: unwrap edek_blob [Workload Identity · Managed HSM]
— skip mint, skip INSERT — same edek_id every call for this name
26b. [FOUND, different app, NOT granted] 403 — request an encrypt grant via /admin/grants or /dek-grants
26c. [NOT FOUND] mint fresh DEK · KEK-wrap · INSERT edek_records (tagged dek_name) — this app becomes its owner
27. { edek_id, wrapped_dek_b64, reused: true|false } [RSA-OAEP-256, wrapped for CLNT's own public key]
28. RSA-OAEP-256 unwrap locally (private key never leaves CLNT) → AES-256-GCM encrypt (fresh IV every call)
29. one edek_id → many rows/values, each with its OWN token (fresh IV per call)
token format identical to HSM Service's own — its real /decrypt reads it with zero awareness of this flow
ciphertext written directly into CLNT's own target table/file — never sent back to HSM Service
NamedDekRotationScheduler (age-based, default 30d) periodically retires "found" rows above — new lookups then fall to 26b
One scheduler instance covers rows from BOTH /encrypt and /dek/issue (same process, same edek_records table) — no separate SVC scheduler needed since the merge
30. BULK File job specifically: each chunk's plaintext is base64-encoded before AES-256-GCM — survives HSM Service's own /decrypt UTF-8 response encoding losslessly
FileBulkJob.reconstructCoreServiceToken(edek_id, iv, tag, ciphertext) — same token format as line 29 above, now true for files too, not just DB columns
Optional compress-before-encrypt: each chunk gzipped, then a 1-byte raw/gzip marker prepended inside the base64 — decrypt always reads it, encrypt-side-only config
CoreBulkFileInteropTest (hsm-bulk-client, real hsm-core-service process) — encrypts via /dek/issue, decrypts via HSM Service's real /decrypt, both directions + compression, every build

31. hsm-spark-adapter shares this exact flow via hsm-crypto-client's SvcClient/DekManager — same /dek/issue, /dek/unwrap, and RSA-OAEP-256→AES-256-GCM steps above, driven from Spark UDFs (hsm_encrypt/hsm_decrypt) instead of a batch job
